note: Literature confirms CLN3 pathogenic variants can cause isolated, nonsyndromic retinitis pigmentosa without juvenile neurodegenerative manifestations, requiring genetic testing to distinguish from other nonsyndromic RP forms.

evidence.text: Biallelic CLN3 pathogenic variants can lead to isolated, nonsyndromic retinal degeneration presenting as rod-cone dystrophy without the severe neurodegeneration typical of juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Biallelic variants in CLN3 lead to a spectrum of diseases, ranging from severe neurodegeneration with retinal involvement (juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis) to retina-restricted conditions.

numbers.metric: nonsyndromic IRD cases harboring biallelic CLN3 variants

evidence.text: Patients with CLN3 mutations can present with isolated nonsyndromic retinal degeneration spanning ages 16 to 70 years without systemic neurologic features, exhibiting rod-cone dystrophy patterns.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: A multi-institutional case series of 10 patients who presented with isolated nonsyndromic retinal disease and mutations in CLN3. Patient ages ranged from 16 to 70 years; duration of follow-up ranged from 3 to 29 years.

numbers.metric: patients with isolated nonsyndromic retinal disease
